tasks.task: Write a sourcing plan and a request pack

items.when: When a new product, service or supplier is needed, or a contract is up for re-tender
When a buying need must become a one-page plan and a request suppliers can answer
When starting a spend category cold, to get a supplier list, scoring rules and talk points
When the request is for a made product, to word it in maker terms with checks to run
When you need a first list of suppliers with links you can check
Before the pack is sent, to read it as a supplier and list what they would have to ask

tasks.task: Put quotes on one basis and score the suppliers

items.when: When quotes differ in unit, quantity, currency, delivery point or period
When the quotes are for a physical product and need one table with a risk view
When you need a quick table of two or more quotes and the cash each needs up front
When price is not the only test, to weight the criteria and get one pick with reasons
When goods are imported, to test cost per sellable unit after freight and duty
Before the comparison is shared, to catch formula errors and broken links

tasks.task: Estimate the true cost over one to three years

items.when: When set-up, running, support and exit costs must sit beside the quoted price
When two proposals need cost, risk and a clear pick with points to negotiate
When the purchase is an investment, to work out payback, return and risk
When the purchase is software, to find the price rises and renewal traps that change the total

tasks.task: Write the award decision memo and keep the trail

items.when: When the scoring is done and the award must be written up and approved
When the owner must choose, to set out the options, risks and missing facts on one memo
When the memo is drafted, to score it and get the three fixes that matter
When the choice may be questioned later, to keep criteria, scores and approvals together
Before sign-off, to see which mandatory checks still lack proof

tasks.task: Prepare questions for a vendor call

items.when: When a call is booked and there are 30 minutes to prepare questions on price, terms, risk and exit
When the vendor sells software, to draw the questions from scored criteria
When the vendor will hold data or run something critical, to get questions sized to the risk
When the vendor is an AI tool, to flag data-training and liability terms to raise on the call

tasks.task: Plan a supplier negotiation and the opening email

items.when: When a price talk is coming and the alternative, target, fallback and walk-away must be set
Before the call, to get opening lines, questions to ask and what to listen for
When the supplier holds more power, to plan terms, their needs and the order to move
When the talk is about unit price and minimum order with a factory
When cash matters more than price, to work out which payment terms to ask for
Before the call, to sum up the supplier's side and plan the questions that open it up

tasks.task: Prepare a contract renewal brief

items.when: When a renewal is due and the price has crept up
When there is a notice deadline, to plan it and choose keep, renegotiate or replace
Each month, to list renewals and notice dates due, the traps in each and the asks to make
When replacing is a real option, to see what the switch would take before the talk

tasks.task: Check contract terms before signing

items.when: When a contract is ready to sign and the terms that cost later need finding
When the contract is long, to flag risky terms in plain words and when to call a lawyer
When it is a software subscription, to check renewal, price rise, uptime and data terms
When contracts arrive often, to rate each new one and list the clauses to question

tasks.task: Check a supplier before award and at renewal

items.when: When a supplier's identity, owners and sanctions status must be checked and recorded
When factories have answered your questions, to score each and list the red flags
When the supplier handles data or a critical service, to set a risk tier and review their reports
Before the check is filed, to tie every finding to a dated source
When a supplier's claims sound good, to ask what proof stands behind each one

tasks.task: Request samples and score them the same way

items.when: When two or three suppliers are shortlisted and samples must be judged against the spec
When a sample arrives and there is a tech pack, to pass or fail it line by line
When samples go back and forth, to give go or hold each round and stop at three

tasks.task: Review spending and subscriptions for savings

items.when: When the owner wants to know where the money goes and what to keep, cut or renegotiate
Every quarter, in the first two weeks after the accounts close
When there is a list of supplier payments, to group spend and rank the savings chances
When card and invoice exports are to hand, to find duplicate and unused subscriptions
When the sprawl is software, to find duplicate tools and a plan to cut suppliers
When bills are coded each month, to flag odd ones and where a supplier costs more than before
When the totals look fine, to read the ledger line by line and trace each cost

tasks.task: Check energy and utility bills and compare tariffs

items.when: When a fixed contract is ending, bills jumped, or estimated reads and wrong rates are suspected
When savings actions cost money, to rank them by payback
Before the usage and cost trend is shared, to catch broken formulas and wrong totals

tasks.task: Decide bid or no-bid on a public tender

items.when: When a public tender is found and the client must decide fast, then plan a compliance matrix
When weighing several open bids, to get a go or no-go call on each
When the tender pack is in, to sort requirements by must-have and score the fit

tasks.task: Outline a modern slavery statement or answer a questionnaire

items.when: When a UK statement is due or a large customer sends a forced labour questionnaire
Before writing, to find ethics gaps across suppliers and a questionnaire to send them
Before publishing, to make sure every step claimed has a dated record behind it
When the draft is all policy, to check what the business has really done on the ground

tasks.task: Build an operating cost budget and a cash buffer plan

items.when: When past spend is known, to phase next year's running costs month by month
When quiet months strain cash, to get a dated forecast, a downside case and actions
When the owner wants simple rules for the buffer and who to ask early
When there is a savings target, to compare two budgets that cut in different places
Before the budget is agreed, to catch formula errors in the workbook

tasks.task: Score supplier performance each quarter

items.when: Each quarter, to review key suppliers alongside the spend
When there is delivery or uptime data, to score each supplier and claim missed-target credits
When promises and renewal dates are scattered, to track both in one place
When one supplier is key, to plan what to share and how often to meet

tasks.task: Rate supplier risk and plan a backup

items.when: When the business leans on a few suppliers, to score each and list the warning signs
When a failure would stop sales, to rank the risks and write who does what
When a second source exists, to plan how much to order from each
When the plan looks safe, to turn it upside down and ask what would make it fail

tasks.task: Check supplier invoices against orders and receipts

items.when: Before invoices are approved, to match them and list amounts to question
When goods arrive short or wrong, to match order, receipt and invoice and write to the supplier
When invoices come as files, to pull the fields out and match them to purchase orders

tasks.task: Cut the unit cost of a made product

items.when: When a product's margin is thin, to get a cost sheet by part, terms to ask for and a plan
When freight and duty invoices are in, to know the true landed cost per unit first
When the cost sheet shows where to push, to plan the talk with the supplier

tasks.task: Choose a software tool, agency or service provider

items.when: When proposals for a service must be compared on scope, price and risk
When tools are being compared, to score each against needs and list contract checks
When two or three options are close, to have a fresh reader pick against the brief
When the pick replaces a supplier in use, to plan the exit and a staged switch

always.when: Before a request, memo or statement is sent, to catch typos and a supplier named two ways

helpers.when: When a sanctions hit, export control or regulated purchase needs a formal review
When the client decides to bid on a tender and the response must be written
When order sizes, lead times and stock levels drive the buying decision
When freight quotes, Incoterms, customs papers or a 3PL are part of the purchase
When the budget needs cost centres, accruals or a full cost model
When suppliers cannot quote because the spec or tech pack is not yet written

gaps: No library item screens a supplier against OFAC, UK and EU sanctions lists or checks owners and controllers
No library item checks energy, water or telecoms bills for errors or compares tariffs and contract quotes
No library item builds a compliance matrix for a public tender or reads a tender notice for pass or fail rules
No library item drafts a modern slavery statement or answers a customer's forced labour questionnaire
No library item writes an RFI or RFP pack for a service, agency or freelancer; the fits are for made products
No library item works out total cost of ownership over one to three years with set-up, running and exit costs
No library item writes a sample request and a scoring sheet when there is no tech pack
No library item writes question lists for a vendor sales call outside software
No library item sets a purchase approval policy with limits, or a simple purchase order process
No library item benchmarks a quoted price against market rates or builds a should-cost estimate
